title: Raycast2D unpredictable behaviour on edge of collisionshape without ignoring it
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible with example project in: 4.5.beta4, 4.5.beta3, 4.4.1.stable, 4.3.stable, 4.2.2.stable ### System information Godot v4.5.beta4 - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7260) - AMD Ryzen 9 5900X 12-Core Processor (24 threads) - 63.88 GiB memory ### Issue description When using a Raycast2D, either with a `intersect_ray` from the `.get_world_2d().direct_space_state` or a Raycast2D node, when the raycast is not a child of a collisionshape and right on its edge facing outward, certain orientations make the raycast hit and some not. This ignores the `hit_from_inside` property. When offsetting the raycast slightly outside or within the object makes it not trigger, as well as rotation all the nodes together in certain orientations. This seems like some sort of floating point imprecision, especially when rotating manually. Strangely, when trying to rotate the parent Node2D with a script, the raycasts do not trigger at all. From testing, it seems like only the raycasts down and right are a problem, so the positive directions of the axis. (all raycasts in this image have `exclude_parent` enabled, and `hit_from_inside` disabled, the ones with a child label are children of the staticbody) I came across this when doing a pong like game and predicting bounces of the ball. When using the direct_space_state to raycast until collision, getting the normal and using that to "bounce" the raycast further only worked on the bottom wall. To solve it, I had to seperate out the two walls into seperate staticbodies to exclude each after a hit. It might be possible to offset the ray starting point a tiny bit, but you would have to make sure to not just move along the edge. But that is undesirable when trying to precisely raycast. The fact that further inside the body is "okay again", is also pretty unintuitive. According to a comment from 2021 in #55873, this might already be a known issue and maybe intended behaviour or too hard to fix. That was the only issue that I found actually adresses this issue, but I wanted to bring it up again since it feels very much not intended and also confusing when encountering it. tldr: a raycast might wrongly trigger right on the edge of a collisionshape in certain situations ### Steps to reproduce - create a parent `Node2D` - create a `StaticBody2D` - create a `CollisionShape2D` with a rectangular shape (e.g. (100,20) in size) - create a `RayCast2D` as a sibling to the `StaticBody` - set the `RayCast2D` right on a bottom or right edge of the `CollisionShape2D` (in this example on (0, 10) facing down) - in debug settings, set the Collisionshapes to visible - start the project and see the raycast change when manually rotating the parent `Node2D` ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [raycast-test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21511151/raycast-test.zip)
